textbookText: B. Separation of sand Take the given mixture of sand and common salt in a beaker. Add sufficient water little at a time stirring continuously with a glass rod to dissolve the common salt.
Warm the mixture solution gently. Allow the sand to settle down by standing the mixture for sometime.
Then, decant off the supernatant clear liquid. Add water, and repeat this process 3-4 times.
Now fold the filter paper as shown in figure and fit into the funnel.
Fit the apparatus as shown in figure. In this process, the stem of the funnel should touch the inner wall of the beaker whereby there will be no loss of liquid.
Transfer the supernatant liquid into the funnel by means of a glass rod. The filter paper should not be filled more than 2/ 3rd of it.
Add a little water in the beaker. Allow the mixture solution to stand for some time to settle and filter off the supernatant liquid. Repeat this process 2-3 times.

Take few drops of filtrate in a test tube directly from the stem of the funnel. Add few drops of silver nitrate solution. Formation of a curdy white precipitate indicates the presence of common salt in sand.
If a curdy white precipitate is seen, wash the sand again and treat the fresh sand-washed water with few drops of AgN03 solution. Repeat the process of washing till no any precipitate is seen.
Transfer all the sand on to the filter paper.
Remove the filter paper carefully from the funnel. Spread it over the wire gauze.
Dry the sand over the Bunsen burner or in air oven.
Evaporation C. Evaporate the solution of the common salt (filtrate) in a basin to I. dryness to get the solid common salt.
Collect all the common salt on a filter paper.

RESULT
Sand, camphor and common salt were separated from their mixture by the sublimation process followed by filtration, washing and evaporation.
PREtAUTIONS All the glasswares should be handled with care.
The filter paper wrapped outside the funnel should be moistened respectively.
While moistening the filter paper, the sand should not get wetted.
The funnel should cover whole of the mixture in the basin.
While filtering, glass rod should be used and the solution should not come upto the brim of the filter paper.
Note: It's better to wash the sand with little amount of water many times than with a large amount of water.

EXPERIMENT NO. 9
Object: TO TEST WHETHER WOOD-ASH CONTAINS AND
SOLUBLE SUBSTANCES
APPARATUS REQUIRED

THEORY

The presence of soluble substances in the wood-ash can be known by dissolution of the wood-ash in water followed by filtration and evaporation. Filtration can be defined as the method of separafing the insoluble component and solution of the soluble component of the mixture by means of a porous medium like filter paper, glass wool etc. The insoluble component is obtained on the filter paper as residue whereas the solution of the soluble component iS collected below the funnel as filtrate.

Evaporate the filtrate to dryness. If any solid residue is found left in the basin, it shows the presence of soluble matters in the wood-ash.
